blogs.title: E-Cancellation 101: The Fifth Circuit's Update on 'Receipt' Standards in Insurance Statutes
blogs.description: An analysis of how the Fifth Circuit reinterpreted the Louisiana 'receipt' requirement for policy cancellation notices. This post breaks down the tension between statutory language demanding physical delivery ('compliance with private carrier') and the modern reality where computerized server triggers function as 'receipt.' It explores whether federal courts are ready to expand the definition of 'receipt' to include electronic notifications from finance institutions, potentially reshaping how digital data is treated in property law obligations.

blogs.title: The Certification Sphinx: When Federal Courts Refuse to Expound on Ambiguous State Statutes
blogs.description: A deep dive into the Fifth Circuit's procedural ruling to decline certifying questions regarding insurance premium finance statutes. The article examines the court's reluctance to defer to state supreme courts when statutory terms like 'certifying' remain undefined. This post analyzes the 'reservaers policy' and its impact: how federal appellate courts maintain control over state law interpretation when the state system lacks a clear answer, and the implications for future insurance litigation where plaintiffs seek state-level clarification.

blogs.title: Strict Adherence and the Prejudice Note: Can Statutory Formalism Defeat a 'Good Faith' Breach Claim?
blogs.description: Examining the substantive consequences of the *Williams v. GoAuto* opinion on insurance contract disputes. The ruling dismissed claims with prejudice due to statutory non-compliance, highlighting the 'strict adherence' doctrine found in Louisiana case law. This post analyzes the chilling effect of such formalism on equitable claims like good faith and fair dealing, arguing that strict adherence to duplication notices in a financing context can preempt broader, more plaintiff-friendly consumer protection theories.
